props.title: Drive Me Crazy

sections.content: Drive Me Crazy (1999) sits perfectly within the late 90s teen movie renaissance, alongside She's All That (1999) and 10 Things I Hate About You (1999). Starring Melissa Joan Hart and Adrian Grenier, it follows the classic fake-dating plot that dominated teen comedies of the era. Like Clueless (1995) before it, the film cleverly updates classic literature - loosely inspired by "Pride and Prejudice" - while capturing authentic teen dynamics of the pre-social media age. The chemistry between Hart and Grenier particularly stands out, avoiding the typical "makeover miracle" trope by letting both characters genuinely evolve.

sections.content: The film's soundtrack, headlined by Britney Spears' "(You Drive Me) Crazy," exemplifies the symbiotic relationship between teen movies and pop music in the late 90s. This era gave us iconic soundtrack moments like "Kiss Me" in She's All That (1999) and "Can't Take My Eyes Off You" in 10 Things I Hate About You (1999). Drive Me Crazy continues this tradition, using music to amplify emotional beats while creating a perfect time capsule of 1999 pop culture.

The fake relationship plot device gained particular traction in 90s teen films, seen also in Whatever It Takes (2000) and Never Been Kissed (1999). What sets Drive Me Crazy apart is its equal treatment of both main characters' social worlds - neither the popular crowd nor the alternative scene is portrayed as entirely right or wrong, adding surprising depth to what could have been a shallow premise. sections.content: Drive Me Crazy marks a transition point between the more innocent teen films of the early 90s like Don't Tell Mom the Babysitter's Dead (1991) and the more sexually aware teen comedies that would follow, like American Pie (1999). It maintains a relatively clean approach while still addressing real teenage concerns about identity, popularity, and authenticity. This balance would influence later films like A Cinderella Story (2004) and Mean Girls (2004).
